html:
SMTO-EXE-0278 — A command in this task's terminal needs your attention first

GUID: 9fab760d-7bbe-4330-ba49-58ba573c44ac
Slug: workspace-terminal-attention-required
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: terminal-handoff

What happened

  • SMTO didn't start a new step because a command already running in this task's terminal is still using something that step needs, and it has gone quiet. That command is still running and wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task and look at the command running in its terminal. If it shows a question or prompt, type your answer there. The command has been quiet, which can mean it is waiting for an answer, though it may simply still be working.
  2. If you see Let agent handle next to the terminal wait, select it to let SMTO answer, or select Wait indefinitely to leave the command running untouched. These controls decide who responds to the quiet command without stopping it.
  3. Wait until that terminal command shows it has finished, then ask SMTO for the new step again. The new step needs something the running command still holds, so it can only start after the command ends.

What success looks like

  • The terminal command shows as finished, and the new step starts when you ask for it.

If it still fails

  • Don't start the same command again, and don't retype an answer you're unsure was received; that could make it run twice. If the command seems stuck, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A new immediate action was rejected before execution because a live workspace terminal job in the same task holds a conflicting resource lock and has a ready or consumed silence handoff.

What this means

  • A new action was rejected before execution because a live workspace terminal job in the same task holds a conflicting resource. That job has an outstanding or delivered silence handoff. Silence does not establish a failure or prove that input is required. Its original process and resource ownership are preserved.

Why this can happen

  • A live terminal job in the same task holds the requested resource after a terminal handoff.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the blocking job identified by the no-start receipt. A second pager or prompt may appear in that same process.

How to fix it

  • Use manage_job logs or inspect on the blocking_job_id from the rejection, send input with manage_job action=input if a prompt is waiting (a pager may need text='q', submit=false), then wait on that same job until it completes before requesting the conflicting action again. A second prompt can appear in the same job, so confirm completion first.
  • Inspect the existing terminal job and answer any prompt there. Wait for that job to complete before requesting the conflicting action again.

Retry and execution caution

  • The original terminal job has completed or its resource ownership has been safely resolved.

How to verify the fix

  • The original job reaches a confirmed terminal outcome, and a subsequently requested action can start.

What not to do

  • Do not relaunch the existing command or resend input whose delivery is uncertain.

Technical notes

  • This rejection does not cancel the original job, release its locks or replay either command.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
